title: Scientific Opinion on the evaluation of allergenic foods and food ingredients for labelling purposes
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the Food Safety Authority of Ireland (Question No EFSA-Q-2011-00760). Prevalence data were reviewed under EFSA procurement project CT/EFSA/NDA/2012/02.
authorConflicts: Declarations of interest of panel members are held by EFSA; not read.
result: Cow's milk contains about 30 to 35 g protein per litre; chymosin or acidification to pH 4.6 separates whey and casein, which hold about 20% and 80% of milk proteins. Caseins: alpha-s1 12-15 g/L, alpha-s2 3-4 g/L, beta 9-11 g/L, kappa 3-4 g/L. Caseins bind calcium through phosphoserine or phosphothreonine residues of alpha-s1-, alpha-s2- and beta-casein, forming nanoclusters with amorphous calcium phosphate stabilised by kappa-casein, which aggregate into micelles. Whey: beta-lactoglobulin 3-4 g/L, absent from human milk and relatively resistant to acid and enzymatic hydrolysis; alpha-lactalbumin 1-1.5 g/L. Caseins are not significantly affected by severe heat treatment.
